plan: In a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value, regardless of others’ strategies. This maximizes expected profit because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Discrete $0.1 increments don’t change this conclusion. With value $29 and only one round (no signaling/learning), bid 29.0. Ties are random, but truthful bidding remains optimal.

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values (uniform 0–49), bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding can cause losses if others overbid; underbidding risks losing positive-profit wins. There’s no prior history to exploit (round 1/1). Therefore, bid exactly your value: $30.0.
